title: Immunohistochemical Expression of Claudin 1 & 3 in Various Odontogenic Cysts
author: Safa Fathy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t4seqwe
materials: Claudin-3 is widely expressed in a variety of normal and neoplastic tissues. In normal tissues, claudin -3 was immunoexpressed in normal epithelia of intestine, kidney, liver, skin, lung, and in endothelia, as well as in the blood–brain barrier (Wolburg et al, 2003). Furthermore, Ibrahim et al (2007) detected immunohistochemical expression of claudins 1, 4, 5 and 7 in the human dental germ.

Siar et al (2013) evaluated the immunohistochemical expression and localization of five tight junction proteins or claudins (1, 3, 4, 5, and 7) in the keratocystic odontogenic tumor (KCOT) and compared it with dentigerous cysts (DCs) and radicular cysts (RCs). Furthermore, they correlated their immunohistochemical expression with the biological behavior of the studied lesions. They observed marked claudin-3 loss of expression in KCOT basal layer compared with DCs and RCs. they suggested that claudin-3 downregulation might indicate altered or loss of basal cell polarity and impaired barrier function of KCOT lining epithelium. In contrast, they pointed out that the distribution patterns of claudins 1, 4, 5, and 7 were less distinctive; suggesting that these molecules probably play limited roles in influencing the different growth potentials of all the examined lesions. In Conclusion, their findings suggested that differential claudin expressions in the lining epithelium of KCOTs, DCs, and RCs probably reflect their neoplastic or nonneoplastic nature.
The aim of the present work is:
Transmitted light microscope and computerized image analyzer.

steps.title: Select tissue cases
steps.instruction: Select a total of 40 paraffin‑embedded tissue samples, comprising 10 radicular cysts, 10 odontogenic keratocysts, 10 unicystic ameloblastomas, and 10 ameloblastomas.

steps.title: Cut sections for H&E
steps.instruction: Cut each paraffin block into 4 µm‑thick sections and place them on slides for routine hematoxylin‑and‑eosin (H&E) staining.

steps.title: Cut sections for IHC
steps.instruction: Cut parallel sections from the same blocks and mount them on positively charged microscope slides for immunohistochemical staining.

steps.title: Perform routine H&E staining
steps.instruction: Stain the 4 µm sections with standard hematoxylin and eosin protocols to confirm histopathological diagnosis.

steps.title: Perform claudin‑3 immunostaining
steps.instruction: Carry out immunohistochemistry on the positively charged slides using monoclonal antibodies directed against claudin‑3.

steps.title: Assess immunostaining
steps.instruction: Evaluate the immunostained slides by two predefined assessment methods (details of the methods are not specified in the source).

steps.title: Analyze and tabulate data
steps.instruction: Collect the image‑analysis results, tabulate all data, and perform statistical evaluation as described in the study plan.
